title: A comprehensive analysis reveals the potential risks and molecular connections between aspartame and polycystic ovary syndrome.
authors: Huang, Zebin; Xie, Lingna; Zheng, Xinyu; Lu, Yu-Jing; Huang, Jia-Jun; Zhou, Jin-Lin; Huang, Mingtao
one_liner_zh: 该文用网络毒理学和分子对接/MD研究阿斯巴甜与PCOS关联，虽涉及TF（FOS/JUN）结合但对象为小分子-蛋白，非蛋白质-DNA互作体系，方法可迁移性有限。
abstract: The widespread use of aspartame has raised increasing health concerns, particularly regarding its potential endocrine-disrupting effects and a possible association with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), a condition marked by endocrine and metabolic abnormalities. This study systematically investigated the molecular mechanisms by which aspartame may contribute to PCOS pathogenesis using a network toxicology approach. A total of 281 common targets between aspartame and PCOS were identified. Protein-protein interaction network analysis and five topological algorithms revealed 20 hub targets significantly enriched in pathways such as endocrine resistance, TNF signaling, and progesterone-mediated oocyte maturation. Eight of these targets showed significant differential expression in PCOS patients. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) further demonstrated that several of these hub targets are embedded in co-expression modules positively associated with PCOS phenotypes. Transcription factor prediction indicated that these targets are primarily regulated by FOS and JUN. Molecular docking showed favorable binding affinities between aspartame and both transcription factors. Subsequent molecular dynamics simulations supported the dynamic stability of aspartame binding to FOS and JUN. These findings suggest that aspartame may contribute to PCOS by modulating FOS- and JUN-mediated transcriptional programs, thereby disrupting biological pathways related to endocrine regulation and inflammation. Collectively, this study reveals a potential mechanism by which aspartame mediates PCOS and offers novel insights for toxicological assessment of food additives.
abstract_zh: 阿斯巴甜的广泛使用引发了越来越多的健康担忧，尤其是其潜在的内分泌干扰效应以及与多囊卵巢综合征（PCOS）的可能关联，后者是一种以内分泌和代谢异常为特征的疾病。本研究采用网络毒理学方法，系统探讨了阿斯巴甜可能促进PCOS发病的分子机制。共鉴定出阿斯巴甜与PCOS之间的281个共同靶点。蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用网络分析和五种拓扑算法揭示了20个枢纽靶点，这些靶点显著富集于内分泌抵抗、TNF信号传导和孕酮介导的卵母细胞成熟等通路中。其中8个靶点在PCOS患者中表现出显著差异表达。加权基因共表达网络分析（WGCNA）进一步表明，其中多个枢纽靶点嵌入与PCOS表型正相关的共表达模块中。转录因子预测显示，这些靶点主要受FOS和JUN调控。分子对接显示阿斯巴甜与两种转录因子之间具有有利的结合亲和力。随后的分子动力学模拟支持了阿斯巴甜与FOS和JUN结合的动态稳定性。这些发现表明，阿斯巴甜可能通过调节FOS和JUN介导的转录程序，从而破坏与内分泌调节和炎症相关的生物通路，进而促进PCOS的发生。总体而言，本研究揭示了阿斯巴甜介导PCOS的潜在机制，并为食品添加剂的毒理学评估提供了新见解。
